mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% month-over-month signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND HOUST MoM change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of at least 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by more than 1% in a month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decrease of at least 0.25 percentage points in FEDFUNDS and a concurrent increase of at least 0.5% in CPIAUCSL signals a failed rate hike, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS MoM change < -0.25% AND CPIAUCSL MoM change > 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 2% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a concurrent decline of more than 1% in personal income (PAYEMS) signals a precautionary savings regime, which reduces consumer spending and weighs on corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS MoM change > 2% AND PAYEMS MoM change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during periods of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.5%) indicates that labor market weakness in a low-inflation environment is associated with equity market resilience due to central bank accommodation.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE and 20-day S&P 500 forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during periods when CPIAUCSL < 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of at least 1.5% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during months when INDPRO rises by more than 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
